key_insight: A nickel-based weld metal with approximately 0.5 wt.% tungsten achieved high strength and impact toughness at −196 °C, with potential raw material cost savings of 10–20%.
engineering_relevance: The consumable could offer a lower-cost welding option for cryogenic LNG storage systems without sacrificing the reported mechanical performance.
method: Developed nickel-based weld metal with substantially less tungsten than conventional ERNiCrMo-4.
Evaluated deposited weld metal strength and elongation.
evidence_signal: The abstract reports 510 MPa yield strength, 746 MPa tensile strength, 40% elongation, and average Charpy impact energy of 169 J at −196 °C.
watch_item: The abstract does not establish full-joint qualification or verified production cost savings; both require validation before LNG service adoption.
paper_title: Development of a Cost-Effective Nickel-Based Welding Consumable for Cryogenic LNG Storage Applications: Mechanical Properties and Impact Toughness at −196 °C
